pages.name: Route III: The Wild Road
pages.html:
The purple route cuts south through Cericas and Fangoth, crosses the difficult country toward Solace, then continues through Haven and Pax Tharkas before turning toward Wayreth.

LegNormal timeExpected window
Vogler → Cericas5–7 days25–27 Darkember
Cericas → Fangoth3–4 days28 Darkember–3 Frostkolt
Fangoth → Solace7–10 days7–12 Frostkolt
Solace → Haven2 days9–14 Frostkolt
Haven → Pax Tharkas2–3 days11–17 Frostkolt
Pax Tharkas → Wayreth4–6 days20–25 Frostkolt

Reading These Windows

Every window above is an arrival window for a normal journey, and each already includes the short stops described on that leg's page. They are not best-case figures. The whole-route totals below are the ones to quote at the table.

How the journey goesDays from VoglerReaches WayrethAgainst the 26 Frostkolt deadline
Aggressive — mounted, minimal stops24–2816–20 FrostkoltSix to ten days spare
Normal adventuring pace28–3320–25 FrostkoltOne to six days spare
On foot with serious delays33–3625–28 FrostkoltOn the deadline or past it

Route Identity

This is the adventurer’s road: shortest line, least dependable infrastructure, highest chance that a local problem becomes a full session. It should feel earned when the party reaches places other travelers reach by safer means.

Shortest distance between two points is a straight line. This useful piece of mathematics was clearly invented by someone who had never travelled through Lemish.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 1: Vogler to Cericas — Leave the Good Roads
pages.html:
Five to seven days carries the party out of the comfortable assumption that every night ends at an inn.

Travel Beats

  1. The Last Reliable Signpost. A road marker gives clear distances; later markers do not.
  2. Cold Camp. Make weather and good equipment matter before true wilderness danger appears.
  3. The Returning Travelers. A small group coming north describes Fangoth without telling the party not to go there. Their restraint is more unsettling than a warning.

Information

  • Cericas is the last comfortable stop before the route becomes politically and physically uncertain.
  • Fangoth can be entered; starting a fight there is another matter.
  • Food, rope, winter clothing, and spare footwear are more valuable on this route than luxury gear.

pages.name: Stop 1: Cericas — Last Roof Before Lemish
pages.html:
Cericas is the final place where a warm bed, cooked food, and simple directions can all be assumed on the same evening.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
25–27 DarkemberHalf sessionResupply, warnings, local character scenes

Arrival

Keep Cericas modest. Its importance is emotional and logistical, not political. Locals know that travelers headed south are either very experienced or very optimistic.

Campaign NPCs

  • Hett Marrow: innkeeper who sells food packs and refuses to sell false confidence.
  • Vessa Crow: hunter who can mark two reliable water sources on Ispin’s map.
  • Tomel Darn: merchant who came through Fangoth and paid every toll without complaint.

Scenes

  1. The Missing Scout. A local guide has not returned from checking the southern trail.
  2. Last Chance Market. Give the party a concrete chance to buy supplies they will later wish they had.
  3. The Fangoth Rules. A traveler explains local expectations: declare weapons, pay tolls, do not assume Solamnic rank means anything.

Eat something cooked. Sleep beneath a roof. Beyond here, both become increasingly negotiable.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 2: Cericas to Fangoth — Border Rules
pages.html:
The route now becomes a question of whether the party can move through dangerous territory without treating every unfamiliar authority as an enemy.

Travel Beats

  1. Toll Stones. Old markers have been repainted by different authorities over the years.
  2. Mercenary Camp. Armed travelers are not automatically hostile; they are selling information, escort, and loyalty.
  3. The Wrong Uniform. Someone wears Solamnic equipment with insignia removed. The explanation matters.

Time

Detouring around Fangoth can add 2–3 days and should not be treated as a free way to avoid local politics.

pages.name: Stop 2: Fangoth — Law of the Iron Gate
pages.html:
Fangoth is one of Route III’s defining sessions. The party can enter, trade, learn, and leave—if they accept that local law is not Solamnic law.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
28 Darkember–3 FrostkoltOne full sessionHobgoblin politics, trade, Krell entrance, route identity

Arrival

Fortifications, mercenary traffic, armed merchants, and disciplined gate procedure make Fangoth feel dangerous without requiring immediate violence.

Campaign NPCs

  • Magistrate Vark Ironledger: cares about order, tolls, and contracts more than species prejudice.
  • Keska Nine-Nails: mercenary broker who can sell a guide toward Solace at a painful price.
  • Rellin Voss: Lemish trader who knows which roads are being watched by Dragonarmy sympathizers.

Scenes

  1. Declare Your Steel. Every weapon is recorded at the gate. Hidden weapons become a serious legal problem if discovered.
  2. Krell in Custody. He may be a prisoner accused of espionage, forbidden magic, or carrying stolen papers.
  3. The Contract Board. The party can earn legal favor by solving one local problem instead of attempting a jailbreak.

Knowledge Available

  • The path toward Solace is passable but unreliable.
  • Mercenaries and collaborators know the war is coming before isolated villagers do.
  • Someone has offered coin for information about travelers carrying High Sorcery markings.

Do not start a fight in Fangoth. Finish one if necessary.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 3: Fangoth to Solace — The Hard Section
pages.html:
Seven to ten days make this the longest and least predictable overland leg of the Wild Road.

Break the Leg into Three Movements

  1. Leaving Fangoth. Roads exist but are watched and politically dangerous.
  2. The Wild Middle. Forest, bad tracks, water crossings, old ruins, and navigation become the main threats.
  3. Approach to Solace. Signs of trade and habitation return, making the vallenwoods feel like a genuine arrival.

Travel Challenge

ResultEffect
Strong success7 days; arrive with supplies intact.
Mixed8–9 days; one supply or equipment cost.
Failure10 days and a one-day-equivalent complication already included in the leg.
Major detourAdd 1–2 days beyond normal.

pages.name: Wild Leg Set Piece: The Road That Is Not a Road
pages.html:
Use this when the party needs a memorable wilderness session between Fangoth and Solace.

Hook

A visible track seems to offer a full day’s shortcut. It is real, but it was made by smugglers and later abandoned after something changed in the woods.

Scenes

  1. Choose the shortcut with incomplete information.
  2. Find a deserted smuggler camp containing useful supplies and one disturbing map.
  3. Cross a ravine where the old bridge has been deliberately cut.
  4. Discover why the road was abandoned: monster, magical anomaly, hostile patrol, or haunted ruin.

Time

Success saves no full day but keeps the party at the fast end of the 7–10 day window. Retreating after deep commitment adds one day.

pages.name: Stop 3: Solace — The Last Home
pages.html:
Solace is a reward for surviving the hard leg and a temptation to forget the calendar for one comfortable night too many.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
7–12 FrostkoltHalf to one full sessionRest, classic Dragonlance atmosphere, information, emotional pause

Arrival

Vallenwood trees, elevated structures, familiar roads, travelers, and the Inn of the Last Home should feel almost impossible after the wilderness.

Campaign NPCs

  • Maris Tanglebough: traveler who knows Haven Road and gives directions that are actually useful.
  • Old Fen: remembers Ispin ordering potatoes and telling an obviously false story about how he reached Solace.
  • Lira Dawn: young mage who has heard that Wayreth is “near” but cannot find two people who agree where.

Scenes

  1. The Inn. Let the party have a proper meal and character scene.
  2. The Map Wall. Travelers have pinned route notes that contradict one another near Wayreth.
  3. The Temptation. Offer something genuinely fun that requires staying an extra day. Make the choice real.

Go to the Inn. Order the potatoes. This is not a suggestion.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Leg 4: Solace to Haven — The Road Returns
pages.html:
Two days on an established road should feel almost luxurious after the wild middle.

Use the Contrast

Wagons, milestones, traffic, and predictable camps return. The danger shifts from navigation to people, rumor, law, and the spreading effects of war.

Scenes

  1. A merchant train asks to travel together for safety.
  2. Seekers or local officials question travelers about magic.
  3. A southbound messenger carries news that makes the party reconsider how much time remains safe to spend in civilization.

pages.name: Stop 4: Haven — Crowds, Law, and Rumor
pages.html:
Haven should feel busier, more commercial, and more ideologically tense than Solace.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
9–14 FrostkoltHalf to one sessionMarkets, law, religious tension, war rumor, resupply

Arrival

Give the party choices: shops, information, official records, religious speakers, transport, and people claiming to know exactly what the party should believe.

Campaign NPCs

  • Speaker Joran: local Seeker official suspicious of unsanctioned magical claims.
  • Vela Marr: merchant who can outfit the party for colder mountain travel.
  • Terin Ash: courier carrying a partial report about military movement toward the east.

Scenes

  1. Public Debate. A robe-wearing traveler is accused of causing a magical disturbance they did not create.
  2. Map Seller. A vendor sells “guaranteed” Wayreth maps, all different.
  3. The Pax Tharkas Question. Locals disagree whether the old route is safe, politically sensible, or simply faster.

pages.name: Leg 5: Haven to Pax Tharkas — The Land Rises
pages.html:
The road climbs and the architecture of the past begins to dominate the landscape.

Travel Beats

  1. Mountain Weather. A fast-moving cold front makes shelter matter.
  2. Old Stone. The party begins seeing ancient work that dwarfs modern roadside structures.
  3. Shared Road. Traders, pilgrims, soldiers, and displaced families all use the same narrow passages.

Time

Two to three days normally. A blocked pass, damaged bridge, or military inspection can add one if mishandled.

pages.name: Stop 5: Pax Tharkas — The Citadel of Peace
pages.html:
Pax Tharkas is the Wild Road’s great historical image: proof that earlier peoples built monumental things because cooperation once seemed possible.

Expected windowSuggested playPrimary function
11–17 FrostkoltHalf to one full sessionHistory, scale, political symbolism, final major threshold

Arrival

Slow down the description. Twin towers, mountain walls, dwarven engineering, elven artistry, and the sense of old agreements should make the party stop thinking only about miles.

Campaign NPCs

  • Archivist Kel Tor: carries copied historical records and can identify references to Wayreth that contradict modern maps.
  • Rinna Vale: guide who knows the next practical stretch but refuses to claim she can find the Tower.
  • Sergeant Korr: watches travelers moving through the old route and has noticed someone asking after the party.

Scenes

  1. The Old Inscription. A historical text describes Wayreth relationally rather than geographically.
  2. The Closed Passage. A minor structural collapse forces teamwork or a delay.
  3. The Pursuer’s Trace. Evidence proves the party is no longer the only group using their route.

Adventurers become so accustomed to ruins that we sometimes forget people once built things because they believed the world might become better.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Final Leg: Pax Tharkas to Wayreth
pages.html:
Four to six days should strip away the last confidence the party gained from reaching famous landmarks.

Progression

  1. Day One: useful tracks and known terrain.
  2. Day Two: trail forks absent from every map.
  3. Day Three: a stream crosses the road twice without turning.
  4. Day Four: the party sees smoke from its own previous camp ahead.
  5. Day Five/Six: the Forest begins responding to behavior, memory, or magical allegiance rather than direction.

You cannot simply find Wayreth. The Forest must allow you through. So when the road disappears, do not panic. When it appears somewhere else, follow it.

— Ispin Greenshield

pages.name: Route III: d12 Wild Encounters
pages.html:
The Wild Road has the highest encounter rate, but even combat encounters should tell the party something about the land or the war.

d12Encounter
1A mercenary patrol offers safe passage for coin and accurate intelligence for more coin.
2A frightened family is hiding from people wearing no consistent uniform.
3Wild dogs or wolves trail the party but retreat from something deeper in the forest.
4A bridge is intact but a toll collector has no legal authority beyond the armed companions standing nearby.
5A wounded hobgoblin courier carries Fangoth legal papers and a message about Dragonarmy recruiters.
6A campsite contains warm ashes, no travelers, and an Ispin story scratched into a tree.
7An abandoned wagon holds winter supplies and a journal explaining why its owner fled on foot.
8A magical animal watches the party from impossible distances for two consecutive days.
9A patrol has arrested a robe-wearing traveler as a suspected spy.
10The route disappears beneath sudden flooding; finding a new crossing is a travel challenge.
11A group of pilgrims insists Pax Tharkas is safer than Haven and refuses to explain why.
12At moonrise, every compass points toward a different direction for one minute.

pages.name: Route III: d12 Rumors and Intelligence
pages.html:
Rumors on the Wild Road come from mercenaries, refugees, smugglers, isolated villages, and people who may not have any reason to tell the truth.

d12Rumor
1“Fangoth will let anyone in who pays. Getting out is the complicated part.”
2“Somebody is buying prisoners with magical tattoos.”
3“The shortest trail to Solace changes after heavy rain.”
4“The Inn of the Last Home has the best potatoes in Ansalon.”
5“Haven is arresting people for saying the old gods are returning.”
6“Pax Tharkas was built to prove elves, humans, and dwarves could share more than a battlefield.”
7“A black-robed traveler passed this way without leaving footprints.”
8“The Dragonarmy pays better than local lords and kills deserters faster.”
9“Wayreth is west of wherever you are standing.”
10“No, Wayreth is south until it decides otherwise.”
11“Ispin once crossed Lemish with no map because someone stole it. He claimed this improved navigation.”
12“Your names have been asked for at two places you have not reached yet.”

pages.name: Route III: Survival, Supplies, and Delay
pages.html:
The Wild Road should make preparation visible without becoming a daily ration spreadsheet.

IssueIf preparedIf unprepared
FoodTravel normallyHunt/forage scene; failure risks exhaustion or +1 day.
ColdNormal restConstitution saves during severe weather.
NavigationKeep fast end of travel windowDrift toward slow end; major failure adds a day.
MountsProtect paceInjury or loss is difficult to replace before Solace.
ShelterAvoid exposureImprovised shelter consumes time/resources.
Local lawPass through Fangoth and checkpointsDetours can add several days.

Reward characters whose backgrounds give them practical travel expertise. The route should prove that noncombat proficiencies matter.

pages.name: Route III: Krell, Skaith, and Mereth in Fangoth
pages.html:
Fangoth gives the pursuit story its strongest political shape.

Krell

Place him in custody, awaiting judgment, sale, exchange, or transfer. The charge can be espionage, forbidden magic, stolen papers, or entering under a false identity.

Ways to Leave with Him

  • Win a legal argument under local custom.
  • Complete a service for Magistrate Vark.
  • Pay a lawful bond.
  • Expose the actual crime Krell is being blamed for.
  • Break him out and accept that Fangoth now has a reason to remember the party.

Skaith

Skaith uses Fangoth’s record-keeping against the party by creating a second set of sightings or impersonating Krell inside the city.

Mereth

Mereth can operate openly through mercenary contacts and may offer to pay the party for the right to end the problem permanently.

pages.name: Route III Signature Adventure: Fangoth — The Iron Ledger
pages.html:
This full session makes the city more than a place where the party either fights hobgoblins or leaves.

Hook

Krell’s release depends on a missing contract ledger that proves somebody has been buying prisoners outside normal law.

Scenes

  1. Question merchants and mercenaries who do not fear the party but respect useful leverage.
  2. Discover the ledger was stolen by somebody trying to expose a trafficking network.
  3. Survive an attempt to destroy the evidence.
  4. Return the ledger, publish it, or bargain with it.

Reward

Krell’s legal release, a Fangoth contact, and evidence that enemy agents are interested in magically marked captives.

Time

Complete before the next morning and it replaces normal rest/resupply time; prolonged pursuit costs one day.

pages.name: Route III Signature Adventure: Solace — One More Night
pages.html:
This social adventure weaponizes the route’s greatest temptation: comfort.

Hook

A celebration, reunion, contest, or local mystery offers no strategic benefit at all. It is simply something the characters would enjoy.

Purpose

After danger and scarcity, give the players a genuine reason to spend a day because their characters are alive. The campaign clock only matters if leisure is sometimes worth considering.

If They Stay

Advance the date one day and reward the choice with relationships, information, inspiration opportunities, and an NPC who may matter later.

If They Leave

Do not punish them. Let the empty road at dawn feel like the cost.

pages.name: Route III: Optional Adventures and Expansion
pages.html:
The Wild Road naturally supports the longest version of the opening arc.

LocationAdventureCore question
CericasThe Missing ScoutHow much danger should the party accept before the “dangerous part” even begins?
FangothThe Iron LedgerCan the party work inside hostile-looking law rather than immediately reject it?
Fangoth–SolaceThe Road That Is Not a RoadIs a promised shortcut worth entering a place locals abandoned?
SolaceOne More NightIs time only valuable when spent advancing the quest?
HavenThe Accused MageWill the party intervene in a public injustice when doing so draws attention?
Pax TharkasThe Closed PassageWhat does cooperation look like when ancient cooperation is literally built into the walls?

pages.name: Route III Finale: The Shortest Road Was Never Short
pages.html:
The Wild Road should end with a sense that the party crossed more than distance: they learned to navigate people, wilderness, law, uncertainty, and themselves.

Expected Arrival

ConditionsWayreth window
Aggressive and clean — 24–28 days16–20 Frostkolt
Normal — 28–33 days20–25 Frostkolt
Several serious delays — 33–36 days25–28 Frostkolt

Final Image

Ispin’s purple line ends at a point the party can physically reach. The actual road continues into trees that do not appear on any map. Behind them: Cericas, Fangoth, Solace, Haven, and Pax Tharkas. Ahead: a place that does not care how straight the line looked on parchment.

The shortest distance between two points was never the same thing as the shortest journey.

— Ispin Greenshield
